_about: Every sentence the legibility review page draws (D-066, D-025.8). A number is a {token} gen-legibility-review.mjs fills from the inputs; a {{token}} is filled by the page itself when it runs (counts of your choices, the page's sha). A typed number stops the build, a JSON number too. Ids that carry a number (L-01, R-11, D-066, P1, G1, EX-5, a review finding id, r1) and HTTP statuses are labels, not counts.

page.h1: Round 1 of your human reading: what changed, what you choose, and the patterns behind it
page.lede: You read all-endpoints on {ep} as a person, one hover at a time, and raised {nItems} items. Each was logged in your words, fixed, then reviewed. This page shows what changed, the looks you pick by seeing, your questions answered, the gap analysis you asked for, and the patterns that made the page clear to a model but not to you.
page.source: Pictures are real clicks on the page (the walk). Facts are read from {app} @{feedHead}. The work reviewed is at {workHead}.

glance.itemsHead: Your items, by where they stand
glance.itemsNote: Counted from each item's status in the ledger. {withOpt} of them also leave a look for you to pick.
glance.findNote: The review read round 1 through {nLenses} lenses and wrote {nFindings} findings. Round 1b worked each one.

glance.measNote: Each check counts one kind of defect on {ep} at {viewport}. It is a prototype of a suite check: it reports, it stops nothing.
glance.take: Take from this: {built} of your {nItems} items are built and {opts} leave a look for you to pick. Of the {nCompared} checks the measure compares, {down} went down from before to round 1b, {same} stayed and {up} went up.

calls.title: Your calls
calls.note: Every look added this round, grouped by where it lives on the page. Each look has its picture from the walk. The dashed one is my pick; a filled one is yours. Click a look to make it yours; click it again to give it back.
calls.motionNote: Choosing a look makes it the page's default, marked ruled in the words file. The other looks stay until you say to drop them.
calls.take: Take from this: {nCalls} looks wait for you ({nRuled} already ruled) and {nProps} proposals need your yes or no. Pick by the pictures; a look you leave stays my pick, never a ruling.

items.title: Your items
items.note: One card per item, in your order: your words, where, what changed, what the review found after round 1, and what round 1b closed.
items.take: Take from this: after round 1 the review still found something on {partlyItems} of your {nItems} items; round 1b fixed {closed} of the {itemFindings} findings tied to them.

qs.title: Your questions, answered
qs.note: Plain answers. Every number is read from the feed when the page is built.
qs.take: Take from this: every answer is about the code except the last, which is about the map. That is why it sits here and not on the page.

gap.title: The gap analysis
gap.note: You asked for a gap analysis between the lab's {nParts} parts and the page's {nNew} sections (L-19). Here it is, counted from its record: {nRows} rows, {nNone} with no home yet.
gap.take: Take from this: the page carries the lab's parts except {nNone} rows with no home yet. Security is the gap: {secMissing} facts are missing from both, {secOrphan} sat in rows that are leaving. My pick, G1, adds no ninth row: a Security control lights the security items across the rows.

pat.title: The patterns
pat.note: Why the page was clear to a model and not to you, grouped. One card per pattern, the biggest first: how many of your items and of the review's findings it holds.
pat.landNote: Nothing here lands in the suite before you say “land it” (D-066). Each proposal is a draft; your choice is the word.
pat.pickRule: My pick: land it where something of the pattern is still on the page after round 1b (an open item, or a finding fixed only partly or left); not yet where nothing is.
pat.take: Take from this: {nPatterns} patterns; the biggest, “{topPattern}”, holds {topN} of your items and the review's findings together. My pick is land it on {nLand} of them, and each waits for your word.

rem.title: Still on the page
rem.note: What is still on the page after round 1b, by pattern. Honest: these are the patterns coming back on new surfaces.
rem.take: Take from this: {nOpen} of {nRem} are still open. They came back on surfaces built after the rules were written, by agents who had been told the rules. That is the reason for P10.

copy.title: Copy
copy.note: One line per choice, grouped calls · proposals · patterns. A note you write rides on its choice's line.
copy.take: Take from this: paste the text back to me. A line that says my pick is never a ruling.

questions.q: Why do these items have no icon?
lines: Before this round, an item wore an icon only when the Gabe Universe draws a node of its kind. It draws functions, tables, schemas, hooks and middleware. It draws no rate limit, check, fork or catch, so those were bare words.

Now each gate names the function or the middleware it runs in, with that element's icon and role. The gate itself wears an icon of this page's own, one per kind; which icons is one of your calls (gate icons).
A function always wears the function icon now, even when no role is known for it.
Items without an icon in BY MOMENT on {ep}: {bareBefore} before this round, {bareNow} after round 1b. In the Gates row: {gateBefore}, then {gateNow}. In Functions: {fnBefore}, then {fnNow}.
What the measure still finds without one: {bareNowRows}.

questions.about: sensitive and global, at the edge
questions.verdict: Q: what is this — a function?
lines: No. {sName} and {gName} are {nLim} counters, objects of the class {limClass}. The server builds them once, when it starts ({mwFile}: line {initS} for {sName}, line {initG} for {gName}).
They belong to {mwName}, a middleware: code every request passes through before any endpoint runs. Its method {mwMethod} asks each counter if this client's IP is over its limit.
{sName}: the {sPrefixN} path prefixes on its sensitive list, this one among them ({sEndpoints} endpoints). At most {sLimit} requests in {sWindow} seconds. Checked at line {sLine}, first.
{gName}: every path but {gExempt} ({gEndpoints} endpoints). At most {gLimit} requests in {gWindow} seconds. Checked at line {gLine}, after {sName}.
Over a limit, the answer is {limStatus} “{limDetail}” and the endpoint never runs. Both counters run only when rate limiting is switched on, or in production ({limSwitch}).

questions.q: What is fetching, and from where?
questions.about: the client hook after the answer
questions.verdict: Q: what is fetching and from where?
lines: The hook that sends this request is {sender}, a {senderKind}. It sends {sendMethod} {sendPath}.
When the answer is a success ({invWhen}), it refreshes the saved answers under the key {invKey} ({invAt}). A refresh throws those answers away, so a screen that shows them fetches them again.
{nRefetch} hooks keep a saved answer under that key, so this is what is fetched: {refetchList}.
This request writes {writes}. {readsList}

questions.q: Why do the 403 and the 404 trigger? In which context?
lines: Each ending has a cause in the server and a branch on the screen.
@statuses

questions.q: What are we representing in standard or specialist?
questions.verdict: Q: what are we representing in standard or specialist?
lines: The row answers one question: is this endpoint built like the others, and what is unusual about it?

An endpoint is made of pieces: its method, each status it can answer, reading a body, its login, its rate limit, its catches, its switches, a repeat key. Each piece is counted across the app's {nEp} endpoints. The rule: {pieceRule}.
{ep} has {nPieces} pieces: {nNorm} the norm, {nCommon} common, {nRare} rare, {nOnly} only here. It lacks {nLacks} of the norms.
Its rare pieces are what is unusual: {rareList}.

Its switches ({switchKinds}) are not unusual: {switchLine}. A switch is set by the server's settings and changes a way the request can go. So by my pick a switch stands in Gates and decisions beside what it switches, and a rare piece becomes a label on the item it names.
An in-flight value is something the code keeps outside a local variable, so a later moment can use what an earlier moment put there. It is not a flag stored in the database.
This request carries {nInf}: {nReq} go with the answer, {nSrv} are kept by the server between requests.
@inflightReq
Kept by the server: {srvNames}. Of these, {srvDecNames} are read where the {srvDecStatus} endings are checked ({srvDecLines}).

questions.q: Why do these functions have no role?
questions.about: This answer is about the map, not the code, so it lives here and not on the page (D-017).
lines: A function's role comes from the Gabe Universe, and the Universe draws only what the code map reads. The code map reads {nScanned} folders of apps/api: {scannedList}.
@named
Folders the forms feed reaches that the code map does not read: {unreadDirs}.

Where no source knows a role, the page now uses the station's own rule on the feed: accessor when a function reads or writes a table in its own body, gate by the station's name rule. Otherwise a function wears its icon and its name, and its hover says what it does.
The fix is to widen what gustify's code map reads. That is a change in gustify, and it waits: work stays in the suite for now.
